source.title: The Token Before the Value Is the Key: How Hybrid Architectures Organize Induction Circuits
source.authors: Ke Cheng; Xin Xu; Yi-Xiao Chen; Lei Xin; Jian-Bai Zhao; Fan-Hu Zeng; Yue Liu; Jun Zhang; Jie Jiang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests induction-like source preparation and retrieval with layer-update patching, paired probes, and interventions, rather than the original attention-score and in-context-learning-loss measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper measures Carrying, Matching, and Copying, their development over training, and effects on recall. It does not measure loss falling with token index or a training-loss bump. Figures are described in the text, but many plotted profile values are not tabulated; those rows are marked figure_only.
record.test_reason: It measures induction roles (lag-one Carrying, content Matching, Copying, source-key dependence) with block-update patching rather than attention scores. It does this in small Transformers, GDN/SWA/DSA hybrids, pure GDN and released Qwen checkpoints. It also varies training conditions that shift where and when these roles form. It reports no token-index in-context-learning loss, no loss bump and no few-shot task comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that efficient layers carry the token before the value (lag one) into the historical source, and global receivers match it via the source key. Changing early predecessor support (lag-1 mask, convolution removal, early LR) relocates Carrying and Matching and alters natural-text prediction profiles. Window size and enriched text shift functional formation timing, with enrichment mattering mainly for the Transformer.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation patching of block updates, fixed-value selection swaps, source-key restoration, and targeted recall rather than the original attention-score induction-head and token-index loss measurements. The study focuses on hybrid allocation and predecessor-support interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit location and formation timing vary with lag-one versus lag-two support, convolution availability, early learning-rate changes, global-receiver layout, local-window size, training text, and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Pure GDN retrieves associations through query-time recurrent state while historical-source Carrying is near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent-only models can perform associative recall without an induction-style historical-source route.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating matched retrieval heads raises natural-text recall NLL more than ablating control heads, at both original and relocated receivers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-like receivers in hybrids contribute causally to natural-text repeated-association prediction.

record.problems: Several circuit profiles are available only as figures, with exact values not stated in the text. Formation probes track functional responses at selected coordinates and do not measure the in-context-learning loss curve or training-loss bump in V2. Principal controlled conditions generally use three runs; some released-checkpoint and recurrent-only comparisons use one seed.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional layer, intervention, receiver, head, and 318M conditions. They were not individually included because the 60-row limit favors results directly bearing on the listed versions, explicit mixed or null outcomes, and training-condition comparisons. Omitted detailed profiles and pathway comparisons are principally in Figures 3, 5, S3–S7 and Tables S4, S6–S11, S16–S19; omitted additional recall/domain metrics are in Tables S9–S10 and S15–S17.

untested.parts: No attention-only model. Previous-token-head composition via K is traced numerically only in hybrids (Tables S4/S5) and Qwen3.5, not in the small Transformer.
Abruptness, coincidence with an in-context-learning gain, and a loss-curve bump are not measured. Formation thresholds are reported but not related to loss.
Entirely untested; there is no token-index loss measure and no share of ICL attributed to induction heads.
Entirely untested; there is no few-shot task-learning comparison.

Carrying and Matching onsets are tracked separately but cross thresholds in the same or adjacent 0.5–1K bins (Table S12). The resolution cannot show separate sub-steps, and the authors make no such claim.
Only two released 4B checkpoints and a handful of controlled architectures; no other modalities.
Only local-window, convolution, early-LR and one enrichment filter are varied. Whether induction forms at all under data changes is not tested.

missing.what: Transformer Carrying specificity: L3 paired-minus-off-site +1.76/+0.89/+2.43; L6 small or negative
Transformer source-edge dependence: Carrying 2.99 open vs 0.019 closed; Copying 5.79 vs ≈0 (L5→L6)
Transformer fixed-V pattern-only selection at L6 4.24 ± 1.78 and L7 2.40 ± 2.84
Head-level coincidence of source attention, Matching and Copying heads in Transformer and hybrids
Qwen3.5 L18→L19 K restoration recovers 1.420 of 1.444 sender-patch loss; Q, V and gate ≈0
GDN–SWA(16) also lacks historical-source Carrying (<0.02), Matching 0.36
Transformer early LR reduction relocates its circuit and worsens recall (multiple far 25.73→33.60)
Transformer persistent lag-1 head constraint moves peak Carrying to L2 in all runs (baseline L5/L5/L3)
318M hybrid: LR reduction in different groups yields early, intermediate or late routes

record.verdict_notes: Most evidence is from hybrids, so it is credited to V4/V5 rather than V1, which names attention-only transformers. The small Transformer has MLPs and is the closest V1 test; its composition-level results are in unrecorded tables. Formation timing does not test V2 or V7, since no loss or ICL curve is reported and onset resolution is 0.5–1K steps. Several profile values are figure-only. Single-seed results for pure GDN and DSA.

versions.untested_parts: Tests Carrying, Matching, source-key dependence, and Copying in constructed association tasks across several model types. Does not establish the specific previous-token-head composition in all tested models.
Measures functional Carrying/Matching formation timing and its dependence on training conditions; does not measure token-index in-context-learning gain or a coincident training-loss bump.
Does not measure how much of large-transformer in-context learning, defined by loss falling with token index, is carried by induction heads.

Tests several attention, hybrid, recurrent, and sparse-receiver configurations, including released Qwen checkpoints. Does not survey all model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
Tests selected changes to local access, early learning rate, local-window size, and training text. Does not exhaustively map data or training conditions.
Does not compare few-shot task learning with copying or establish which mechanisms mainly carry few-shot learning.
Tracks Carrying and Matching formation separately and compares onset thresholds, but does not establish a general count or formal decomposition of phase transitions.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Pure GDN without global attention (one seed)
labels.reason: R21 limits generalization of the historical-source circuit: Carrying is below 0.02, while query-state transfer reveals an alternative recurrent retrieval route. This does not establish absence of all induction behaviour.

labels.label: supports

labels.reason: The interventions change circuit allocation, formation timing and final recall profiles. R12–R13 require their stated baselines, and R15–R16 require corrected Matching intervals.

labels.label: limits_scope

labels.reason: R17–R18 show modest or no systematic enrichment effects; corrected R15 shows threshold-dependent timing differences; R4–R5 show relocation in only two runs. These qualify specific intervention effects.
